A platform site reliability engineer reports that the ingestion API acknowledges payloads with a 200 before validation, so invalid records fail invisibly with no error surface. Data-completeness SLAs are breached silently and engineers trace losses through logs by hand.

USER STORY:
As a platform site reliability engineer, I want synchronous validation with a structured per-record error report for every rejected payload, So that invalid records are rejected at submission time and never disappear silently.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: Invalid payload accepted with success status
Given a client submits a payload that violates the ingestion schema
When the API responds
Then the response is a 4xx with a per-record error list identifying each violation
And partially valid batches report accepted and rejected records separately
And every rejection is queryable via an errors endpoint for 7 days

PROBLEM STATEMENT: 
The billing support specialist at an e-commerce platform is unable to reconcile the discrepancy between the 'paid' status in the UI and the reminder email sent for settled invoices.

USER STORY: 
As a billing support specialist, I want the system to accurately reflect the status of invoices as 'overdue' instead of 'paid' in the UI, so that I can correctly identify and follow up on outstanding invoices.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 
Scenario: Given the invoice is settled and the dunning system is enabled, When the UI is accessed, Then the invoice status should be displayed as 'overdue' instead of 'paid'.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 
Scenario: The reporting suite's network tab is queried with a comparison across two quarters.
Given: The query is executed on a standard reporting suite instance.
When: The query takes less than 10 seconds to complete.
Then: The reporting suite displays the results without errors or delays.
And: The reporting suite allows for ad-hoc decision-making based on the query results.

PROBLEM STATEMENT: 
The Okta integration causes repeated push prompts on trusted devices, resulting in MFA fatigue and significant time losses for field teams.

USER STORY: 
As a DevOps engineer, I want to minimize the number of repeated push prompts on trusted devices, so that I can reduce the time lost due to MFA fatigue and improve the overall efficiency of the team.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 
Scenario: The Okta integration is configured to use a trusted device list.
Given: The device list is populated with trusted devices.
When: A user attempts to access the system from a trusted device.
Then: The user is not prompted for MFA.
And: The system authenticates the user successfully without prompting for MFA.

A DevOps engineer on an internal tools team reports that authentication on trusted devices becomes a repeated prompt-fest, driving users away from self-service login. The repeated prompts violate the service-level SLA and cause an avoidable onboarding headache.

USER STORY:
As a DevOps engineer on an internal tools team, I want a configurable trusted-device policy that honors the user's stored authentication-state, So that authenticated users on trusted devices are not prompted for credentials every time.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: MFA prompt on trusted device
Given a user authenticates successfully from a device that has been approved by the policy
When the user returns to that device within the trusted-window time frame
Then the session proceeds without an additional MFA prompt
And the trusted-device status is persisted for the duration of the active session

  And the charts are rendered correctly, without empty boxes
  And the board materials are automatically included in the PDF

PROBLEM STATEMENT: 
The billing portal fails to update customer addresses in PDF invoices after the customer has updated their address information.

USER STORY: 
As a procurement analyst, I want the billing portal to update customer addresses in PDF invoices after the customer has updated their address information, 
So that I can ensure accurate and up-to-date billing and avoid rejecting invoices due to outdated addresses.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 
Scenario: A customer updates their address information in the account page.
Given: The customer's new address is saved in the system.
When: The billing portal is run with the updated customer information.
Then: The PDF invoices generated show the customer's new address.
And: The accounting department accepts the invoices without rejecting them due to outdated addresses.

The retry button in the invoicing console generates a new invoice instead of reusing the original.

Given: The original invoice is generated and displayed in the console.
When: The retry button is clicked.
Then: The original invoice is reused and displayed in the console.
And: The new invoice is not generated.

USER STORY:

PROBLEM STATEMENT:
The backend API returns a 429 status code without providing any indication of when to retry, causing unpredictable sync job failures and paging the on-call engineer.

USER STORY:
As a backend engineer, I want the API to return a retry hint or indication when it returns a 429 status code, so that I can diagnose and resolve the issue more effectively.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: The API returns a 429 status code with a retry hint.
  Given the API returns a 429 status code with a "retry-after" header.
  When the API returns a 429 status code with a "retry-after" header.
  Then the "retry-after" header value is provided in the response body.

Scenario: The API returns a 429 status code without a retry hint.
  Given the API returns a 429 status code without a "retry-after" header.
  When the API returns a 429 status code without a "retry-after" header.
  Then an error message is returned in the response body indicating that a retry is not possible.

USER STORY:
As a backend engineer on the integrations team, I want standard rate-limit headers including Retry-After on every 429 response, So that clients can honor rate limits deterministically instead of guessing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
Scenario: Rate limit response omits retry-after header
Given a client exceeds its API rate limit
When the API returns a 429 response
Then the response includes Retry-After plus quota and reset headers
And successful responses include remaining-quota headers for the current window
